input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Midstream repository onboarding for the Platform Operator

## Description

Creates the midstream repository for the Platform Operator component under the
opendatahub-io organization, giving the FIPS compliance work for this
component a code landing place. The Platform Operator has no
architecture-context file in the platform inventory, so it is treated as a new
component and receives the standard onboarding chain; this epic is the
repository-creation step of that chain.

## Scope

- Create the midstream repository for the Platform Operator sources under
  opendatahub-io, following the established midstream forking workflow used by
  other platform components.
- Establish the default branch structure and the upstream synchronization
  workflow.
- Wire basic repository CI so that pushes to the midstream repository are
  validated from day one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream repository exists under the opendatahub-io organization and
  contains the Platform Operator sources.
- A clean clone of the repository builds successfully and basic repository CI
  runs green.
- The upstream synchronization workflow is configured and documented in the
  repository.

## HLR Traceability

Enables HLR-1 (P0) for the Platform Operator: the FIPS crypto remediation of
its images needs this repository to exist. Prerequisite onboarding work — no
direct HLR mapping.

# License validation for Platform Operator dependencies

## Description

Runs license validation over the Platform Operator's transitive dependencies
so that licensing problems are found before the FIPS-compliant images are
built, not after. This is the license-scanning step of the onboarding chain
for the Platform Operator, which has no architecture-context file in the
platform inventory and is treated as a new component.

## Scope

- Run license scanning over the full transitive dependency tree of the
  Platform Operator sources.
- Triage findings: identify any dependency licenses incompatible with
  shipping the component in Red Hat OpenShift AI product images.
- Resolve or document remediation for every incompatible license finding
  (replacement dependency, exception request, or removal).
- Record the scan results and decisions so they can feed later compliance
  evidence work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The license scan covers the complete transitive dependency tree of the
  Platform Operator sources.
- Every finding is triaged with a documented resolution; no unresolved
  license blockers remain for shipping the component's images.
- Scan results and decisions are recorded in a form reusable by the
  compliance evidence effort.

## HLR Traceability

Enables HLR-1 (P0) for the Platform Operator: remediation of its images
proceeds on a validated dependency set. Prerequisite onboarding work — no
direct HLR mapping.

# Konflux build pipeline onboarding for the Platform Operator

## Description

Onboards the Platform Operator midstream repository to Konflux so its
container images are built by the standard platform build pipeline. The
pipeline produces the signed build attestations that the FIPS 140-3 compliance
evidence package requires, and hosts the gating FIPS-regression check for
this component's builds.

## Scope

- Onboard the Platform Operator midstream repository to Konflux, following the
  standard known-recipe onboarding used by other platform components (KServe
  is already Konflux-onboarded).
- Configure the image build for the Platform Operator container images.
- Verify that builds complete and produce signed build attestations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Konflux build pipeline builds the Platform Operator container images
  successfully (pipeline green).
- Builds produce signed attestations for the built images.
- The pipeline is ready to host the component's gating FIPS-regression check
  once the crypto remediation work lands.

## HLR Traceability

Enables HLR-1 (P0) and HLR-2 (P0): the remediated Platform Operator images
are delivered through this pipeline, and its signed build attestations feed
the compliance evidence package. Prerequisite onboarding work — no direct HLR
mapping.

# FIPS crypto remediation of KServe serving images

## Description

Makes the KServe serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto
in the request path. This epic also authors and verifies the part of the
gating CI FIPS-regression check that covers KServe builds, so regressions
cannot be reintroduced.

## Scope

- Audit the KServe serving-stack images for non-validated cryptographic
  library usage in the request path, producing a per-image module inventory
  (this inventory is a deliverable that feeds the compliance evidence
  package).
- Remediate all identified non-validated crypto usage so the images use
  validated cryptographic modules.
- Verify correct operation of the serving stack on FIPS-enabled clusters
  (functional behavior and crypto correctness).
- Author and verify the gating CI check covering KServe builds: a check that
  fails any KServe serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto
  usage (HLR-3, KServe surface).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every KServe serving-stack image in scope runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster with no non-validated crypto in the request path,
  verified by test.
- The per-image module inventory of crypto usage is produced and handed off
  for the compliance evidence package.
- The gating CI check is wired into the KServe build process and
  demonstrably fails a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all KServe serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
  clusters using validated crypto modules.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the gating CI check covering KServe builds is authored
  and verified here because it spans the same build surface this epic
  remediates — a standalone CI epic would audit the same builds twice.

# FIPS crypto remediation of Platform Operator images

## Description

Makes the Platform Operator's images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift
clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto
in the request path. This epic also authors and verifies the part of the
gating CI FIPS-regression check that covers Platform Operator builds. It
starts once the component's midstream repository exists and its dependency
licenses have been validated (both are prerequisites of the onboarding chain
for this newly onboarded component); the Konflux build pipeline onboarding
proceeds in parallel, and its readiness is enforced by an acceptance
criterion below rather than a blocking dependency.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator images for non-validated cryptographic library
  usage in the request path, producing a per-image module inventory (a
  deliverable that feeds the compliance evidence package).
- Remediate all identified non-validated crypto usage so the images use
  validated cryptographic modules.
- Verify correct operation of the Platform Operator on FIPS-enabled clusters
  (functional behavior and crypto correctness).
- Author and verify the gating CI check covering Platform Operator builds: a
  check that fails any Platform Operator build that reintroduces
  non-validated crypto usage (HLR-3, Platform Operator surface).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every Platform Operator image in scope runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster with no non-validated crypto in the request path,
  verified by test.
- The per-image module inventory of crypto usage is produced and handed off
  for the compliance evidence package.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Platform Operator is green with the
  remediated images (build-pipeline coupling as an acceptance gate).
- The gating CI check is wired into the Platform Operator build process and
  demonstrably fails a build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images, including the Platform Operator, run
  correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the gating CI check covering Platform Operator builds
  is authored and verified here because it spans the same build surface this
  epic remediates — a standalone CI epic would audit the same builds twice.

# Compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving
stack — module inventory, build attestations and test results — and submits
it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification lab. This epic starts after the crypto remediation of both
serving-stack components has landed, because the package documents the
remediated state. The Konflux build pipeline onboarding for the Platform
Operator proceeds in parallel; the attestations it produces are consumed as
content via an acceptance criterion, not a blocking dependency.

## Scope

- Assemble the module inventory from the per-image crypto inventories
  produced by the remediation work on both serving-stack components.
- Collect signed build attestations produced by the Konflux build pipelines
  for all serving-stack images.
- Collect the FIPS test results demonstrating correct operation on
  FIPS-enabled clusters.
- Validate the package internally for completeness and consistency.
- Submit the package through the security review board at its defined
  milestones and to the external accredited certification lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the module inventory, the signed build
  attestations produced by the Konflux build pipelines for all serving-stack
  images, and the FIPS test results.
- The package passes internal validation for completeness and consistency.
- The package is submitted through the security review board at the defined
  milestones and the board's triage feedback is addressed.
- The package is submitted to the external accredited certification lab and
  its intake is confirmed.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the
  security review board meets on a fixed cadence — both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. Certification
  being granted is therefore not an acceptance criterion of this epic; the
  epic's engineering completion point is a complete, validated, submitted and
  intake-confirmed package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

# FIPS support posture documentation

## Description

Documents the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster
prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, through the
Red Hat documentation content process. This is substantive new documentation
authored after the implementation work it describes, so it is scheduled last.

## Scope

- Author new documentation topics covering:
  - the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack (what runs on
    FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules, and what the CI
    FIPS-regression gate enforces);
  - cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation.
- Publish the topics through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documentation topics state the FIPS support posture and the cluster
  prerequisites accurately.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented remediation
  and CI enforcement (review confirmed by the implementing teams).
- The topics are published through the Red Hat documentation process.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites. Epic priority is P0 per the docs-authoring priority
  exception (strategy frontmatter priority Critical → P0).
